user.title: Connect Washington Gas
user.description: Sign in with your My Washington Gas email and password, the same ones you use at my.washingtongas.com. If you made a separate account on the Home Energy Analysis site (wgl.opower.com), that login works too.

data_description.energy_unit: Home Assistant has no therm unit. "Therms" keeps the same numbers as your bill (labeled CCF in the Energy dashboard). "kWh" converts them exactly (1 therm = 29.3071 kWh). This can't be changed later without removing and re-adding the integration.

reauth_confirm.title: Washington Gas password
reauth_confirm.description: The saved password for {username} stopped working. Enter the one you use at my.washingtongas.com now.

error.invalid_auth: Washington Gas didn't accept that email and password. Check that they work at my.washingtongas.com.
error.mfa_required: My Washington Gas asked for a verification code. The integration can't enter codes, so it can't sign in to this account automatically.
error.captcha_required: My Washington Gas is showing a CAPTCHA on sign-in. The integration won't try to get around it, so it can't sign in right now.
error.handoff_failed: Signed in to My Washington Gas, but couldn't get from there to the usage site. Run scripts/check_connection.py from the integration's GitHub page and share its output in an issue.
error.cannot_connect: Couldn't sign in to Washington Gas. Try again in a few minutes. If it keeps happening, run scripts/check_connection.py from the integration's GitHub page to see which step fails.
error.no_accounts: That login worked, but no gas accounts are linked to it yet.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check the Home Assistant logs.

abort.already_configured: This Washington Gas login is already set up.
abort.reauth_successful: The new password works. Washington Gas is reconnected.
